answers.explanation: The housefly has sponging and lapping mouthparts that suit it to liquid food.
Only the male toad has vocal sacs, which amplify its call.
Mosses, liverworts and ferns are all seedless plants.
Thallophytes have a thallus body made of filaments, which both Spirogyra and Mucor show.
Spiders have no antennae, unlike centipedes, crustaceans, millipedes and insects.
The fern prothallus is the gametophyte, which is not the dominant plant; the sporophyte is dominant.
Chloroplasts occur only in plant cells, so they are not common to plants and animals.
Genes are the factors that determine characters in living organisms.
Mercuric and mercurous nitrates give a red colour on heating with protein, which is the Millon test.
The placenta is the organ through which nourishment and oxygen diffuse into the embryo.
Label M is the superior umbilicus, the opening at the top of the quill where the feather shaft begins.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from high to low concentration.
Enzymes are denatured at high temperatures, so they cannot withstand them.
The dorsal and anal fins help fish control rolling movements.
The earthworm has no exoskeleton, unlike maggots, mosquito larvae, caterpillars and termites.
Platelets release substances that start the clotting of blood.
Pepsin breaks proteins down into peptones in the stomach.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces carbon(IV) oxide and ethanol.
Rhizomes are underground stems that grow horizontally through the soil.
A child of a normal AA and a SS parent with sickle-cell trait has the genotype AS.
The biuret test uses copper sulphate solution, which gives a violet colour with protein.
The pancreas secretes enzymes that digest starch, proteins and fats, so its removal affects all three.
Tapeworms fasten themselves to the intestine using hooks and suckers.
The young chick develops from the germinal disc, labelled 2 in the egg.
The yolk and albumen provide food for the developing chick.
All mammals have seven cervical vertebrae, so the rabbit, rat and man have equal numbers.
The piliferous layer is not replaced by cork in old roots; it is the cork layer that replaces it.
A monoecious plant bears male and female flowers, so both the androecium and gynoecium are on the same plant.
A pollen tube contains three nuclei: the tube nucleus and two male gamete nuclei.
Sap is a transport fluid rather than a waste product.
The cerebellum controls muscular coordination, so a very active animal with good muscular control has a well-developed cerebellum.
Webbed feet are adapted for swimming, not for flight.
A transect shows how organisms are distributed along a line across a habitat.
Ascaris reproduces only sexually, so asexual reproduction does not occur in it.
Fehling's solution turns from blue to red when warmed with a reducing sugar.
Blood never flows from arterioles to the artery, because the flow runs from artery to arteriole.
Heat produced in respiration is a waste form of energy that is not used for work.
The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column and ribs, not the limbs.
Blood clotting starts when blood is exposed to air, then fibrinogen becomes fibrin, which forms a network that traps blood cells.
Green plants are producers, which make food by photosynthesis and support all other organisms.
An anemometer measures wind speed.
Nitrogen is an inert gas that makes up most of the air, so it is not a pollutant.
Wind, altitude, humidity and light are all abiotic (non-living) factors.
Smallpox is a viral disease that causes skin blisters and spreads through close contact with an infected person.
Ridging across the slope slows the flow of water and reduces erosion.
In settling, the lightest particles, humus, settle last and the heaviest, stones, settle first, in the order humus, silt, clay, sand, stones.
Denitrifying bacteria release gaseous nitrogen from soil nitrates.
Leaching is the washing out of soluble materials such as chalk and limestone from the upper soil layers by heavy rain.
Soil erosion usually begins as sheet erosion, then develops into rills and finally gullies.
